articles.title: MCP Authorization: Protect an MCP Server with OAuth 2.1
articles.excerpt: Originally published at GeekCoding101. You put an MCP server on an HTTP port, and now anyone who can reach that port can call your tools. That is the problem MCP authorization solves, and the spec's a…
articles.body: Originally published at GeekCoding101 . You put an MCP server on an HTTP port, and now anyone who can reach that port can call your tools. That is the problem MCP authorization solves, and the spec's answer is OAuth 2.1 plus a small discovery document. This post covers what the spec requires, how the 401-to-token flow works, and how to wire it up with the Python SDK. I ran a small demo server and show the real curl output. If you're new to the protocol itself, start with what is an MCP server . One honest caveat up front: the demo uses a fake hard-coded token and a placeholder issuer ( auth.example.com ). There is no real authorization server behind it, and I did not run the full authorization code flow.
articles.author: chaogetalks

articles.title: Zero-Cost Types? The Fine Print on Kotlin Value Classes
articles.excerpt: Compose’s own Dp, Color and TextUnit are value classes. Here's why. @JvmInline value class ShipmentId(val raw: String) reads like a free upgrade: a real type in the source, a plain String at runtime.…
articles.body: Compose’s own Dp , Color and TextUnit are value classes. Here's why. @JvmInline value class ShipmentId(val raw: String) reads like a free upgrade: a real type in the source, a plain String at runtime. Most of the time that is exactly what you get. Sometimes the compiler quietly allocates a wrapper object anyway, and sometimes the erasure itself causes trouble in Room, Retrofit, Java callers or your logs. This post walks through both halves so you can decide where value classes earn their keep. Compose layout and drawing code touches sizes and colors constantly, often many times per frame. Wrapping each one in a heap object would add up, so the toolkit wraps primitive-backed values instead and lets the compiler erase the wrapper. Dp wraps a Float and TextUnit wraps a Long .

articles.title: I built a listing-description tool that starts with the guest, not the granite countertops
articles.excerpt: StayDesc is a small content tool for short-term-rental hosts. You describe your space and amenities, and it returns a guest-ready listing: a hook, the experience framing, friendly house rules, and an…
articles.body: StayDesc is a small content tool for short-term-rental hosts. You describe your space and amenities, and it returns a guest-ready listing: a hook, the experience framing, friendly house rules, and an invite to book. I built it because most listing drafts I saw opened with "beautiful home" and a wall of bullet points, and skipped the one thing that actually books a stay — what it feels like to arrive. The structure is the product The generator follows a fixed shape rather than free-associating. Hook first: one line that names the guest and the feeling, not the square footage. Experience framing: turn "has a kitchen" into "make coffee and watch the ferries". Friendly house rules: stated as hospitality, not as a threat. Booking invite: a closing that asks for the stay.

articles.title: CVE-2026-116606 + CVE-2026-111560: How a Predictable Secret Turns Two Barracuda Bugs Into a Root Shell
articles.excerpt: Barracuda disclosed two flaws on November 2. By November 10, they were being exploited. CVE-2026-116606 (CVSS 9.3) — pre-auth bypass in ESG. An unauthenticated attacker invokes the configuration-impor…
articles.body: Barracuda disclosed two flaws on November 2. By November 10, they were being exploited. CVE-2026-116606 (CVSS 9.3) — pre-auth bypass in ESG. An unauthenticated attacker invokes the configuration-import function and restores a crafted backup archive. No credentials required. CVE-2026-111560 (CVSS 8.6) — command injection in the timezone setting, shared across ESG, Load Balancer ADC, Message Archiver, WAF Control Center, WAF, and Web Security Gateway. The chain: bypass restores a backup with a malicious timezone value → injection fires → root shell. What makes it practical: watchTowr Labs found a static, predictable checksum secret used to validate backup archives. Without it, forged backups fail validation. With it, the archive passes, the config applies, the command runs as root.

articles.title: Did comets bring building blocks of life to Earth? Scientists aren't so sure anymore
articles.excerpt: For over a century astronomers have speculated that comets could have delivered organic molecules necessary for life to Earth, but new modeling shows these molecules wouldn't have survived impact.
articles.body: The origin of life on Earth remains a mystery. New research shows that comets almost certainly did not bring the chemical building blocks of life to our planet. Life as we know it is based around carbon chemistry, also known as organic chemistry. Complex organic molecules are the fundamental building blocks of biochemical compounds such as nucleobases, amino acids, sugars and so on that act as the machinery for biochemistry on Earth . Two big questions are where did this complex chemistry originate? Did these complex organic molecules form on Earth, or were they delivered here from space?

articles.title: NASA's new UVEX space telescope will peer deep into the universe's most violent events
articles.excerpt: NASA's new UVEX space telescope will study the universe in ultraviolet light to reveal the violent and turbulent events that bubble under what appears to be a cosmic sea of tranquility.
articles.body: A new NASA space telescope will study the universe in ultraviolet light to reveal the violent and turbulent events that bubble under what appears to be a cosmic sea of tranquility. The Ultraviolet Explorer (UVEX) mission, developed by NASA in conjunction with the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), will be the first mission to create deep all-sky maps in ultraviolet light. Thus, when it launches in 2031, UVEX will join new sky-mapping surveys like NASA's SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer), which scans the cosmos in infrared, and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, which does the same over the southern hemisphere in visible light, in creating deep-sky maps across a broad swathe of the electromagnetic spectrum.
